verdicts.reason: Once an engagement has started, PATCH takes the started branch. That branch only checks that effective_to is not in the past. It then sets row.effective_to, which can be null or any future date, and saves. It never calls build_employment_engagement_payload, which is the only place the junior next-birthday check (next_rate_review_date) runs. The model's clean() checks only date order, rates and overlap, and nothing else reads next_rate_review_date. So removing or extending the end date succeeds, the junior rates stay, and staff_assignment_defaults will pick this engagement for work after the birthday. The only test calls the payload builder directly and never exercises PATCH.

Creating a successor engagement (or PATCHing one) fires no signal that sets Timesheet.needs_rebuild. signals.py does this for attendance, assignments, leave, MembershipWorkSettings and RosterPeriod, but not for EmploymentEngagement. lock_period only blocks on needs_rebuild=True or on timesheets that are not APPROVED. It then writes the latest revision's stale employment_engagement_public_ids into the manifest and the payroll export. The impact is narrower than claimed: a successor cannot start before today (views.py:311), so only work from today onward in an already-approved open period is affected, usually just today's shift.
